`a4e0c5dca5c6aaab2845f3598935eebf596377dd179b56f781c45d940552f623`.

Reveal time: 2026-09-17 09:52Z, after the blind answer was frozen at `../runtime_context/hotel_reservations_desk/1.md`.

## source_to_kb

### A. Shared surface — base policies, variants, retired clauses

The base-policy sweep (all 15 policies of `policies`, with their `eligibility` blocks, `params`, `formula` entries and `per_tier` tables), the variant sweep (57 parameters × 7 rate plans across the facet documents) and the retired surface (all six `overwrite` entries) are the same single product charter for both tasks of this difficulty. They were audited in full and are set out atom by atom in `./0.md` § A–C. The result, restated here so this file stands on its own:

- **All 15 base policies have a bearing document and are equivalent at the level of entailment.** Checked individually: `stay_agg_multi_holding`, `stay_agg_portfolio_occupancy`, `stay_booking_terms`, `stay_deposit_and_prepayment`, `stay_cancellation` (including the `rooms_given_up_stated` caller-fact eligibility and the `inside_free_cancellation` time eligibility with its complete `temporal_basis` — frozen clock, confirmation-moment anchor, `not_after`, elapsed hours, boundary inclusive, never mixed with calendar days), `stay_no_show_terms`, `stay_room_and_occupancy`, `stay_taxes_and_fees`, `stay_incidentals` (the `stay_in_progress` state eligibility, allowed `[checked_in, checked_out]`), `stay_refund_settlement` (the `reservation_settled` state eligibility, allowed `[cancelled, no_show, checked_out]`), `stay_resort_credit` (the `guest_in_house` state eligibility, allowed `[checked_in]`), `stay_modification`, `stay_evt_property_notice` (the `relocation_approved` authorization eligibility at full strength), `stay_best_rate_guarantee` (the `one_settlement_per_reservation` dedup eligibility), `stay_club_and_corporate_interaction`. Untriggered branches are covered: the full four-band cancellation ladder for all seven plans, the no-show terms, the best-rate terms, the modification schedule and the relocation schedule are all carried although this task triggers none of them.
- **All 57 parameters × 7 plans are carried.** Value-by-value spot check for the plan this task uses, the **Semi-Flexible Rate**, against `variants[].parameters`: `agency_service_fee_usd` 14.95, `breakfast_included` false, `breakfast_fee_per_person_usd` 24.00, `resort_fee_per_night_usd` 35.00, `resort_fee_waived` false, `occupancy_tax_pct` 12.5, `city_tax_pct` 4.0, `parking_fee_per_night_usd` 38.00, `extra_adult_fee_per_night_usd` 35.00, `prepayment_pct` 25, `deposit_nights` 1, `free_cancellation_hours_before_checkin` 72, `refund_processing_days` 10, `room_upgrade_fee_per_night_usd` 95.00, `spa_discount_pct` 5, `overbooking_relocation_allowance_usd` 150.00, `corporate_rate_eligible` true, `club_points_earn_rate_pct` 75 — every figure agrees with the corresponding facet table cell.
- **The retired surface is correct in all three respects.** All six superseded clauses are carried word for word (bar the sentence-final full stop absorbed by the quotation) and written as no longer in force; none survives as a rule in force; none has vanished; and the KB retires nothing the source does not — exactly four documents contain "no longer in force" and they account for all six clauses and nothing else. Each of those four documents re-asserts that the same policy's other clauses stand in force, and those clauses are carried. Two of the six bear directly on this task's chain: the `stay_room_and_occupancy` clause "The room rate is posted night by night and room by room, at the rate the plan was sold at, and a rate once sold is never re-priced …" is retired in *Room Rate and Occupancy Charging on a Hotel Folio*, and the `stay_incidentals` clause "At departure the folio is closed off: every posted line is settled against the deposit already held and the balance is taken from or returned to the card on file" is retired in *Extras Taken at the Property and Posted to a Hotel Folio*. Both are superseded by the current bases this task actually applies, and the KB says so.

**`prerequisite`: empty.** No document of this policy states that its result waits on anything, and the source imposes nothing. ✔

| "the corporate reduction is nil, the length reduction is nil and the advance booking reduction is nil" | "**The three reductions.** The corporate reduction is nil. The length reduction is nil. The advance booking reduction is nil." |
| the ordering: each reduction acts on the figure the previous one left, rounded to the cent at each step, never on the closing rate afresh; "The reductions are never combined into one rate and applied once" | "**The order the reductions act in.**" carries the chain step by step with the rounding at each step, and "**The same ordering put another way.**" restates it; the never-combined sentence is carried verbatim |

## kb_to_source

Every normative claim in the corpus traces to a structured source. The sweep results are the corpus-wide ones reported in `./0.md` § kb_to_source; restated with this task's chain in view:

### Additions — none found

The regex sweep for added-policy shapes (confirmation steps, review steps, notification steps, pointers, exception announcements, ordered step lists) returned **no hits** anywhere in the 68 documents. In particular, none of the four hubs in this task's chain adds a "confirm the figure with the guest", "check the folio again", "notify the corporate account" or "if the settlement fails, follow X" step — the source has no such steps and neither do the documents.

The equivalent restatements in this chain's documents were each checked for smuggled content: *Working Out the Closing Night Charge on a Hotel Folio* restates the ordering twice and its worked example uses an invented 264.00 USD; *Determination of the Closing Tax Charge on a Hotel Stay* restates the exemption's base twice; *Taxable Base of a Closing Hotel Night…* restates its three tiers as a table and then as four worked combinations. None introduces a permitted action, parameter, order or result the source lacks.

### Cross-problem operational guidance — none found

The six hidden tool names occur in exactly six places, one per document, each being that document's own policy's tool named in its own invocation block. ### Omissions / rewrites — none found

Two places in this chain where a boundary could most easily have slipped were checked individually and are exact:

- **The order of the three reductions** on the closing night. A renderer that combined them into one 88 % rate would change the answer from 283.73 to 282.30. The document pins the sequence, the base of each step and the rounding at each step, and states outright that they are "never combined into one rate and applied once".
- **The base the corporate exemption acts on.** A renderer that applied the exemption to the occupancy tax before adding the levy would give a different figure whenever a floor bites. The document states the order and then restates it from the other side.

### Observations recorded, judged not to be defects

- **O1 — "on-site extras" / "on-site charges" is never defined against a record kind.** The source binds both phrases to `event_type='stay_incidental_charge'`. No document says so. The reading is nonetheless forced by the corpus: *Extras Taken at the Property and Posted to a Hotel Folio* governs extras and describes them as taken during the stay and posted "each against the room and the occupant that took them" — and the incidental rows are the only folio rows carrying a non-zero `guest_sequence` — while parking and the property facility fee are governed by a different determination, *Statutory Charges, Facility Fees and Utility Charges on Hotel Stays*, as mandatory per-night charges. The separation is clean at the level of which document governs which charge, so the count resolves uniquely (3 on this folio, 8 on task 0's). The blind audit resolved it correctly and the derived figure matched the gold. Recorded because the boundary is load-bearing — an extras count of 5 would take 18 percent instead of 12 and move the balance by 5.70 — but the semantics the source carries **are** entailed by the visible materials, so this is not an omission.
- **O2 — "occupancy supplement" is the records' `extra_occupant` row and the facet table's "Extra adult, per night" column, and no single document joins the three names.** The join is nevertheless derivable: *Room Rate and Occupancy Charging on a Hotel Folio* says "An occupant beyond the rate plan's standard occupancy is charged the plan's extra-adult or extra-child amount", and the taxable-base factor asks for "the rate plan's occupancy supplement **for an additional adult**", which points at that column unambiguously. Resolved correctly blind. Not an omission.

## Step 4 — policy-side note (does not change this skill's verdict)

**PS-1 — the `stay_ext_closing_tax_charge` baseline rule itself discloses that its taxable base varies.** The source's `baseline.rule` for that policy reads, in part:

> "The occupancy tax is worked out on a taxable base **that may take in more than the room charge alone**, and the city levy is carried with it on one line, no separate city line being raised for that night."

The render contract requires the baseline rule to be carried complete — dropping or softening any of it would be a `KB-BIJECTION RED` — so *Determination of the Closing Tax Charge on a Hotel Stay* carries the sentence verbatim, three lines above its flat default "The taxable base is the closing room charge alone."

The consequence is that this one computation document tells a reader that a broader taxable base exists before any record has suggested one. That is the single thing the discrete-topology design otherwise prevents: the existence of a factor is meant to be discovered from the customer's records alone. The renderer had no faithful alternative and added nothing of its own, so this is **not** a KB verdict against the corpus; the root cause is the wording of the baseline rule on the policy side. Reported here for the source layer to weigh.

Its practical effect on this task is small — the reader is told the base can be broader, but not under what condition, by how much, or which record signals it; the taxable-base ladder's three tiers, its 6-night threshold and its two provisos are all still discoverable only from *Taxable Base of a Closing Hotel Night Where an Occupancy Supplement Stands*, which the reader must reach from the `extra_occupant` rows on the folio. The blind audit reached it that way.

No other policy-side problem was found. In particular, the four `prerequisite` edges of this task are all genuinely unmet at frozen time, all four are state-form with a record-visible state, and no undeclared override or ambiguity was encountered while scanning the whole domain.
